ctx.x: Yeah, as a matter of fact, I will. I've heard about that book.

Because the Duke said essentially the same thing. He said that he had to write his own music because he couldn't remember or didn't care about learning anybody else's, when he tried to get into a bunch of other things, and he found that that wasn't his talent. He just wasn't interested in developing that, and so he became an original composer. And he -- you once said another interesting thing to me, that during the same period, when we were talking about the

orchestration or something. You said, 'to cover up the bones' -- that you wanted to cover the skeleton of the music, because you didn't want anybody to figure out how you did it, or something like that.
